findings.description:
Reentrancy in ZZZVault._receiveVenue(uint256,uint256,uint8) (src/ZZZVault.sol#365-386):
	External call allowing reentrancy:
	- manager.close(p.poolId,p.lpTokenId,deadline) (src/ZZZVault.sol#373)
	Balance read before the call:
	- before1 = _tokenBalance(token1) (src/ZZZVault.sol#369)
	Possible stale balance used after the call in a condition:
	- token0 == address(0) && amount0 != nativeReceived - received (src/ZZZVault.sol#377)
		- stale variable `token0`
findings.rationale: These private helpers run only through guarded Vault financial entrypoints. _balanceUsing spends bounded attributed amounts and checks exact returns; _receiveVenue accepts only the fixed Manager route and distinguishes actual received native credit from a raw ETH balance. Operation 0 allocates fees, 1 closes the complete portfolio, 2 closes only residual; a residual-only close does not clear the main LP ID. Post-callback accounting and idle backing are rechecked. canonicalWrite requires the fixed companion and inert canonical state, so it is not a token-reentry writer during normal operating calls.

findings.rationale: configureNative is direct-governance before/after authorization and native/terminal guarded. _configure invokes only the frozen ActivationAssets child. Its validation uses token/oracle view calls (STATICCALL), then bounded local policy writes; no mutable user-selected callback occurs at admission. Price/admission calls are for revert-on-invalid validation, not use of the returned scalar or policy ID. The new width ceiling remains below10000bps with trigger/deviation coupling. Actual source/venue/governance trust is not proved by the detector.

		- (paid,None) = address(recipient).call{value: msg.value}() (src/ZZZVault.sol#230)
findings.rationale: Captured recipient comes from the immutable Canonical companion and fixed ProtocolPolicy. Constructor rejects zero; proposal validates candidate and acceptance cannot be zero. Sealing validates final recipient; mint binds sale+VRF, exact value and recipient/receiver callback rollback. Repeating a local zero check in the size-constrained Vault would duplicate the fixed source invariant, not close a demonstrated attacker path.

findings.description: ZZZMigration.distributePrincipal(uint256[]) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#269-279) has external calls inside a loop: this.payCurrentOwner{gas: payoutGas}(ids[i]) (src/ZZZMigration.sol#276-277)

findings.description: ZZZMembership.settleDust() (src/ZZZMembership.sol#37-64) has external calls inside a loop: fees.flushDust(bucket,config.key.currency0) (src/ZZZMembership.sol#53)
findings.rationale:
count<=Vault.MAX_BUCKETS=4 is checked. Two fixed current pair currencies per relevant bucket; after compositionEpoch!=0, admitted LP reward currencies explicitly<=33. At most33 unique currencies per bucket and132 flush calls across4 buckets, because the current pair is excluded from the historical-asset loop.
Only bound Vault invokes this economic operation. Snapshot bucket count cannot grow by outside reentry while its Vault contribution is nonreentrant. get/group/epoch/asset reads are static. Fee.flushDust is mutable and independently nonreentrant; it clears dust before credit, requires Vault/Membership and valid bucket status, and preserves canonicalAccounting pre/post checks. Rewards transfers are exact, liabilities updated and backed. A malicious admitted token could revert; it cannot select a new array or receive a sweep.
Bounded incumbent settlement, not an unbounded per-NFT harvest. Funded broken-token dust can block entry atomically; zero dust returns before token handling. Qualify maximum historical-asset gas and exact token behavior.

	Calls stack containing the loop:

findings.rationale:
LP Rewards assets<=33; royalty assets<=17. Royalty activate and syncAll visit<=17; canonical capture/validate/activate visit that ledger limit. CanonicalAdd duplicate checks visit<=33 or17 prior entries. No NFT-supply iteration in this balance helper.
Each balanceOf is static. Royalty activation isolates every optional ERC20 synchronization with a250000gas self-call and120000-tail requirement, preserves old eligible cohort and defers failed currencies; native synchronization has no token call. syncAll and canonical capture/validate/activate deliberately fail atomically if one required currency cannot report backing; per-asset sync remains independently callable. NFT/asset enrollment and ordinary ledger mutation are lifecycle locked during canonical transitions.
Context-specific bounded reads, not globally a harmless false positive. Optional activation faults are isolated; syncAll/canonical availability and max-currency gas remain open dependency/operating qualification.

findings.rationale:
count<=Vault.MAX_BUCKETS=4 is checked. Two fixed current pair currencies per relevant bucket; after compositionEpoch!=0, admitted LP reward currencies explicitly<=33. At most33 unique currencies per bucket and132 flush calls across4 buckets, because the current pair is excluded from the historical-asset loop.
Only bound Vault invokes this economic operation. Snapshot bucket count cannot grow by outside reentry while its Vault contribution is nonreentrant. get/group/epoch/asset reads are static. findings.rationale:

review.call_and_mutation_reasoning: Each balanceOf is static. Royalty activation isolates every optional ERC20 synchronization with a250000gas self-call and120000-tail requirement, preserves old eligible cohort and defers failed currencies; native synchronization has no token call. syncAll and canonical capture/validate/activate deliberately fail atomically if one required currency cannot report backing; per-asset sync remains independently callable. NFT/asset enrollment and ordinary ledger mutation are lifecycle locked during canonical transitions.
review.remaining_risk_or_qualification: Context-specific bounded reads, not globally a harmless false positive. Optional activation faults are isolated; syncAll/canonical availability and max-currency gas remain open dependency/operating qualification.

maximum in1..32; end clamps to exitMintedCount+1, with snapshotted minted count<=1000. Final bucket verification at most4. Completion requires many bounded calls, not1000payouts in one transaction.

findings.description: ZZZMembership.settleDust() (src/ZZZMembership.sol#37-64) has external calls inside a loop: config = pools.get(position.poolId) (src/ZZZMembership.sol#52)
findings.rationale:
count<=Vault.MAX_BUCKETS=4 is checked. Two fixed current pair currencies per relevant bucket; after compositionEpoch!=0, admitted LP reward currencies explicitly<=33. At most33 unique currencies per bucket and132 flush calls across4 buckets, because the current pair is excluded from the historical-asset loop.
Only bound Vault invokes this economic operation. Snapshot bucket count cannot grow by outside reentry while its Vault contribution is nonreentrant. get/group/epoch/asset reads are static. Fee.flushDust is mutable and independently nonreentrant; it clears dust before credit, requires Vault/Membership and valid bucket status, and preserves canonicalAccounting pre/post checks. Rewards transfers are exact, liabilities updated and backed. A malicious admitted token could revert; it cannot select a new array or receive a sweep.
Bounded incumbent settlement, not an unbounded per-NFT harvest. Funded broken-token dust can block entry atomically; zero dust returns before token handling. Qualify maximum historical-asset gas and exact token behavior.

findings.description: ZZZCanonicalHandoff.importRows(uint8,bytes[]) (src/ZZZCanonicalHandoff.sol#299-316) has external calls inside a loop: _module(slot).canonicalImport(row,records[i]) (src/ZZZCanonicalHandoff.sol#312)
findings.rationale:
records.length in1..8 and cursor+length<=recordCount[slot]. Fixed6 slot selector. Ordinary accounting/alias/NFT rows have fixed fields; NFT header includes the immutable pre-seal artworkBaseURI, whose validator restricts scheme but not byte length. Lifetime aliases are processed in8-row chunks rather than one whole-list loop.
Nonreentrant IMPORTING state; source must be EXPORTING with nonzero committed root and same handoffId. Every supplied row hash is compared with sourceModule.canonicalExport at exact ordinal before typed destination import; import cursor increments roll back on any failure. NFT import writes raw ownership without ERC721 receiver callbacks. All ordinary economic activity stays locked.
Bounded iteration, never arbitrary operator accounting rows. A large governance-selected header URI can increase one-row byte/memory/gas cost; actual immutable URI and worst current batch payload must be qualified. Source availability and trusted reviewed replacement behavior still require rehearsal.

ZZZLPBalancer.policyFingerprint(bytes32,bytes32) (src/ZZZLPBalancer.sol#67-80) has external calls inside a loop: (None,None,first) = oracle.priceBounds(address(0)) (src/ZZZLPBalancer.sol#71)

findings.rationale:
Called under at most4 venue candidates and at most12 bounded search passes per candidate. The function has no array traversal itself, just a fixed number of registry/feed/strategy/policy reads.
All dependencies are static. Includes monotonic registry revision, exact target/venue accounting, both source-round fingerprints, execution-quality revision, target ticks/reference and portfolio-control fingerprint. Mutable quote core effects always revert. Manager repeats the captured context after callbacks; callbacks cannot silently swap to a different route policy.
Fixed work per fingerprint but possibly many expensive calls. Approved provider failure/gas can reject a route or entire operation; not a proof of global cheapest routing or worst-case transaction feasibility.

	Calls stack containing the loop:
		ZZZRoyaltyRewards.syncAll()

findings.rationale:
LP Rewards assets<=33; royalty assets<=17. Royalty activate and syncAll visit<=17; canonical capture/validate/activate visit that ledger limit. CanonicalAdd duplicate checks visit<=33 or17 prior entries. No NFT-supply iteration in this balance helper.
Each balanceOf is static. maximum in1..32; end clamps to exitMintedCount+1, with snapshotted minted count<=1000. Final bucket verification at most4. Completion requires many bounded calls, not1000payouts in one transaction.

findings.description: ZZZClaimRouter.claimBatch(ZZZClaimRouter.Claim[]) (src/ZZZClaimRouter.sol#48-74) has external calls inside a loop: IZZZNFT(nft).ownerOf(entry_scope_1.nftId) != msg.sender (src/ZZZClaimRouter.sol#68)
findings.rationale:
1..32 claim tuples. Duplicate nested scan at most496 comparisons, with at most32 payout calls.
Router is nonreentrant and has fixed NFT/royalty destinations. Full owner/duplicate preflight precedes any payout; the second loop repeats current-owner check and each ledger repeats it again. A prior ETH/token payout callback transferring an NFT cannot redirect a later old-owner claim. Ledgers pay the authenticated current owner directly, never router-selected recipient. Any failure rolls the whole batch back.
Bounded atomic claim batch; a failing selected asset/receiver may reject the whole batch. Users may split/omit failing tuples. No universal worst-case payout gas guarantee.

findings.description: ZZZCanonicalHandoff.importRows(uint8,bytes[]) (src/ZZZCanonicalHandoff.sol#299-316) has external calls inside a loop: keccak256(bytes)(records[i]) != keccak256(bytes)(sourceModule.canonicalExport(row)) (src/ZZZCanonicalHandoff.sol#311)
findings.rationale:
records.length in1..8 and cursor+length<=recordCount[slot]. Fixed6 slot selector. Ordinary accounting/alias/NFT rows have fixed fields; NFT header includes the immutable pre-seal artworkBaseURI, whose validator restricts scheme but not byte length. Lifetime aliases are processed in8-row chunks rather than one whole-list loop.
Nonreentrant IMPORTING state; source must be EXPORTING with nonzero committed root and same handoffId. Every supplied row hash is compared with sourceModule.canonicalExport at exact ordinal before typed destination import; import cursor increments roll back on any failure. NFT import writes raw ownership without ERC721 receiver callbacks. All ordinary economic activity stays locked.
Bounded iteration, never arbitrary operator accounting rows. A large governance-selected header URI can increase one-row byte/memory/gas cost; actual immutable URI and worst current batch payload must be qualified. Source availability and trusted reviewed replacement behavior still require rehearsal.

findings.description: ZZZMembership.settleDust() (src/ZZZMembership.sol#37-64) has external calls inside a loop: assets.assetCount() > 33 (src/ZZZMembership.sol#57)
findings.rationale:
count<=Vault.MAX_BUCKETS=4 is checked. Two fixed current pair currencies per relevant bucket; after compositionEpoch!=0, admitted LP reward currencies explicitly<=33. At most33 unique currencies per bucket and132 flush calls across4 buckets, because the current pair is excluded from the historical-asset loop.
Only bound Vault invokes this economic operation. Snapshot bucket count cannot grow by outside reentry while its Vault contribution is nonreentrant. get/group/epoch/asset reads are static. Fee.flushDust is mutable and independently nonreentrant; it clears dust before credit, requires Vault/Membership and valid bucket status, and preserves canonicalAccounting pre/post checks. Rewards transfers are exact, liabilities updated and backed. A malicious admitted token could revert; it cannot select a new array or receive a sweep.
Bounded incumbent settlement, not an unbounded per-NFT harvest. Funded broken-token dust can block entry atomically; zero dust returns before token handling. Qualify maximum historical-asset gas and exact token behavior.

findings.description: The function ZZZRebalanceConfirmation.observe(uint256) (src/ZZZRebalanceConfirmation.sol#192-213) reads (side,identity,manual) = this.condition(bucket) (src/ZZZRebalanceConfirmation.sol#193-212) with `this` which adds an extra STATICCALL.
findings.rationale: The explicit this.condition STATICCALL is required for Solidity try/catch: any fresh oracle/pool/identity read fault must clear observations and emit ObservationReset in a successful transaction. A direct internal call would bubble the revert and undo deletion, restoring stale evidence. Its extra STATICCALL is intentional fault isolation, not an unused convenience call.
